name: gizza-ai/video-first-last-frame-extractor
summary: Grab a video's first and last frame stitched into one comparison image

tool.description: Extract the first frame and the last frame of a video and stitch them into a single comparison image — side by side (horizontal) or stacked (vertical). Both frames are grabbed in one decode pass, so no timestamp is needed. Handy for spotting a clip's start-vs-end change, making a before/after thumbnail, or picking start/end keyframes for AI video tools. Output is one PNG (or JPG) image with the two frames joined; the source dimensions are preserved. Provide the video as either url (HTTP/HTTPS) or ref from a prior tool call. Note: chat ffmpeg is unavailable — runs on the standalone page and the CLI.

format.description: Output image format: png (lossless, crisp) or jpg (smaller file). Default png.

layout.description: How the two frames are joined: horizontal = first frame left, last frame right (side by side); vertical = first on top, last on the bottom. Default horizontal.

ref.description: Reference id from a prior tool call. Use either url or ref.

url.description: Video URL (HTTP/HTTPS). Use either url or ref.
